doc.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Basie walking his bride down the aisle, Joe Williams as best man
summary: He and his wife married in Las Vegas with Basie giving her away and Joe Williams as best man; he also played Williams's hits with the band.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: Interesting. What — have you ever been on a gig when Joe Williams was a guest vocalist?

Oh, yeah, many times, many times. He’s wonderful to work with also. As a matter of fact there’s another bit of Basie memorabilia is that when I was in the band, the lady who was going to be and is now my wife, she and I decided that we were going to get married in Las Vegas because we were going in to play a stint with Tony Bennett at the Sahara Hotel for one or two weeks. And we all agreed. And her father passed away when she was quite young, and so one of the closest friends we had was Basie, and so she asked him if he would walk her down the aisle. We got married at one of these little wedding chapels in Las Vegas. And he agreed. And then we asked Joe and Jillean Williams to be our seconds. And they agreed. So I can in all honesty say Joe Williams was my best man when I got married. It was wonderful. Sarah Vaughan was there, and just all kinds of people. Yeah, I worked off and on with Joe many times with the band, and of course did all the wonderful stuff, “Every Day,” and “Roll ‘Em Pete” and “Comeback” and a lot of all the great, great hits that he had with the band. Of course I knew all of them by heart. I didn’t need any charts on there. But it was really wonderful.
